Definition: from the same as G4730; to hem in closely, i.e. (figuratively) cramp:--distress, straiten.
BiblicalUsage: The word is being hemmed in, pressed on every side. We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed, Paul says, and again, ye are not straitened in us, but ye are straitened in your own bowels: the pressure comes from within, not from the apostles.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the hemmed-in heart is the one that shuts itself up, and the gospel opens what fear closes.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
